cards.title: Fighting resumes in Ukraine's Kherson region after six-day truce
cards.content: Fighting has resumed in Ukraine's Kherson region after a six-day truce, with reports of strikes and injuries. Ukraine's General Staff reported Russian unit rotation, expansion of anti-drone equipment, and ammunition delivery during the ceasefire. The truce was brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump and allowed for the evacuation of hundreds of people trapped in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky. Despite the ceasefire, air strikes continued elsewhere in Ukraine, killing civilians and destroying infrastructure. The unusual show of cooperation between Russian and Ukrainian human rights officials has raised questions about the possibility of more ceasefires and cooperation.

cards.title: US Supreme Court Rejects Trump's Ballot Disqualification Attempt
cards.content: The US Supreme Court swiftly rejected President Donald Trump's attempt to force California to set aside potentially thousands of ballots that the Justice Department claims may have been cast by noncitizens. The court's decision came hours after the appeal was filed and was based on uncertain methodology, which was previously rejected by every court to consider it. The justices did not explain their reasoning, handing down a one-sentence order without asking for a response brief from California or other parties. This marked another major loss for Trump on election cases at the high court, following a previous decision rejecting his plan to change how mail ballots are sent to voters. The Trump administration argued that the federal government has a constitutional interest in ensuring that only citizens vote, while California and voting rights groups countered that the claims are based on fuzzy evidence that risks disenfranchising citizens. Every court to hear the case has now rejected the Justice Department's attempt to cast a cloud of suspicion over eligible voters' ballots on the eve of an election.

cards.title: Giant Bird Fossil Identified as Common Crane
cards.content: Researchers at Bournemouth University have challenged a 150-year-old belief about a giant bird thought to have disappeared after the last Ice Age. Ancient DNA analysis revealed that fossils attributed to Grus primigenia, a supposedly extinct bird species, actually belong to the common crane, a species that still exists in Europe today. This finding raises questions about whether other prehistoric birds classified as extinct species were simply larger forms of birds that survive today. The team led by Dr. John Stewart analyzed DNA from 18 crane bones across England, Wales, France, Germany, and the Balearic Islands to determine the bird's identity. The genetic findings indicate that the oversized fossils belonged to common cranes rather than a separate extinct species. The researchers believe that differences in body size between male and female cranes may have contributed to the original misidentification. The study also leaves another question unanswered: Why were some prehistoric common cranes considerably larger than those living today?

cards.title: South Korea Unveils Largest Budget, Investing in AI and Growth
cards.content: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung presented the country's largest budget ever, promising significant investments in AI and future growth. The budget for 2027 totals 820.9 trillion won, with a 12.8% increase from the previous year. A notable 21.3 trillion won will be spent on semiconductors, physical AI, and AI data centers, nearly double the 2026 level. The government also plans to train 2,000 specialists in semiconductor design, expand AI education, and increase spending on defense and social security. This ambitious spending plan comes as the International Monetary Fund predicts South Korea's economy will grow 3.3% in 2026, its fastest pace since the pandemic. Lee emphasized that the increased spending will not lead to a significant increase in government debt.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: New York reports first measles death in 30 years
cards.content: A child in Lewis County, New York, has died from measles, the state's first measles-related death in 30 years, according to Governor Kathy Hochul. Measles is highly contagious and vaccination is the best protection against the disease. The case is part of a surge in measles cases across the US, with over 4,800 reported this year, the most since 1990. The rise in cases is attributed to falling vaccination rates, although some places have seen an increase in immunizations. The incident has led to renewed calls for vaccination and a reminder of the importance of public health measures to keep people safe and healthy.

cards.title: Professor Thrives on 5 Hours of Sleep due to Rare Genetic Mutation
cards.content: Aimee Pugh Bernard, an immunology professor at the University of Colorado, is one of the few people who can function well on remarkably little sleep, sometimes as little as five hours a night. This is due to a rare genetic mutation called familial natural short sleep (FNSS) which has been linked to short sleep duration in humans. Research has shown that people with FNSS seem to be protected from the negative consequences of short sleep, including memory impairment, and may even experience benefits from their sleep. Scientists are studying the genetic variations associated with FNSS to understand how they work and how they could be used to help people who struggle with sleep disorders. While most adults need seven to nine hours of sleep, genetic factors can influence an individual's sleep duration, with some people being naturally more inclined to need less sleep.

cards.title: Cyclone Murasu Heads for Andhra Pradesh, Landfall Expected November 2-3
cards.content: Cyclone Murasu, a severe cyclonic storm, is barreling towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, expected to make landfall on the night of November 2-3. The storm could cause significant flooding, with storm surges of up to 1.5 meters inundating low-lying coastal areas. Additionally, strong winds of 100-110 km/h and gusts reaching 120 km/h are expected. This storm is notable for its rapid movement across the Bay of Bengal, traveling at speeds of up to 27 km/h. Cyclone Murasu is expected to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, with the India Meteorological Department warning of potential coastal flooding. The storm is being closely monitored by Doppler weather radars in Chennai, Machilipatnam, and Visakhapatnam.

cards.title: Human metabolism's carbon dioxide emissions rise 74% in 30 years
cards.content: A new study by the University of Bath has found that the amount of carbon dioxide produced by human metabolism has increased by 74% over the past three decades, with the global total reaching an estimated 2.05 billion metric tons annually by 2015. The study, published in The Lancet Planetary Health, analyzed thousands of real-world measurements of CO2 production in people of all ages and found that the increase is mainly due to population growth, with more than 60% of the rise attributed to an increase in the number of people rather than a significant change in the amount produced by each individual. The researchers suggest that accounting for this activity could help scientists more accurately predict how effective carbon reduction strategies may be.

cards.title: Srinagar's Water Crisis Worsens due to Climate Change
cards.content: In Srinagar, a water crisis has been ongoing for years, causing daily struggles for residents like Mehak and Zamrood. The absence of a regular water supply has led to the installation of tanks and a hand pump at their homes. Climate change is affecting Doodh Ganga, a vital source of drinking water, causing erratic water supply, low flow, and dry taps. The river's water availability is decreasing due to rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and declining snowmelt. The Kashmir Valley's 24 watersheds, including Doodh Ganga, are experiencing similar impacts.

sections.title: Entertainment

cards.title: SBTV Marks 20th Anniversary with O2 Show Celebrating Jamal Edwards' Legacy
cards.content: SBTV, a pioneering online music channel, is marking its 20th anniversary since its launch by Jamal Edwards in 2006. The platform, known for discovering emerging artists, has helped launch the careers of many successful acts, including Dave, Ed Sheeran, Jessie J, and Skepta. Founder Jamal Edwards, who passed away in 2022, was awarded an MBE for his services to music. His sister Tanisha, now the CEO of SBTV, aims to keep his legacy going by curating a platform that supports up-and-coming talent. To celebrate the milestone, SBTV will host a one-off show at the O2 arena in London, featuring a range of artists, including Tinie Tempah, Lady Leshurr, and Tinchy Stryder, with proceeds going to the Jamal Edwards Self Belief Trust.

cards.title: Rod Argent returns to stage after two-and-a-half-year hiatus
cards.content: The Zombies' founding member Rod Argent, 81, returned to the stage after a two-and-a-half-year hiatus following a stroke. He joined bandmate Colin Blunstone at St Albans Cathedral as part of the band's annual Begin Here Festival, receiving a standing ovation from the audience. Argent initially thought he had suffered a transient ischaemic attack, but hospital tests confirmed it was a stroke. He expressed gratitude for the audience's emotional reaction, saying it was 'very moving.' Argent also praised his wife for her support during his recovery, stating that he wants to spend more time with her, rather than touring again.

cards.title: Courteeners to headline Live at Ludlow Castle with The Coral and The Guest List
cards.content: Indie rock band Courteeners are the latest headlining act to be announced for the annual Live at Ludlow Castle events, joining The Coral and The Guest List as supporting acts on July 16, 2027. The band, known for their 2008 debut album St. Jude, is also promoting their new best-of compilation album, God Bless The Band, which features songs from their seven albums. They will be performing at the concert series, which has been running since 2023 and has seen 50,000 people attend over two weekends. Tickets for the Courteeners will go on sale on November 4 and 6. The band has been together for 20 years and has a history-making album, St. Jude, which took 14 years, 9 months, and 7 days to top the UK chart in 2023.

cards.title: Ryanair Considers Temporary Wage Freeze Amid Fuel Price Spike
cards.content: Ryanair, a major airline, is considering a temporary wage freeze for its staff due to a sharp rise in fuel costs following the US-Israel war with Iran. cards.title: Naomi Nomi Revolutionizes Fashion with Quality, Long-Lasting Clothing
cards.content: Naomi Mishkin, the founder of Naomi Nomi, is revolutionizing the fashion industry by producing high-quality, long-lasting clothing at a higher price point. The average customer starts with one shirt and returns for three more within six months, as they realize the value of her products. Mishkin's approach is a departure from the fast fashion industry, which has mastered the art of cutting production costs to the bone. She uses cotton and wool, making her shirts pricier than fast fashion, but lasting longer. Naomi Nomi's success is attributed to the growing backlash against companies that prioritize profit over quality and the environment. The fashion industry has undergone significant changes over the past few decades, with a shift towards planned obsolescence and the use of cheaper materials. However, some consumers are now looking for brands that offer quality, durability, and sustainability, and Naomi Nomi is capitalizing on this trend.

cards.title: Nscale to Build UK's Largest AI Data Centre in Loughton, Despite Microsoft Pullout
cards.content: Nscale, a tech company, has reaffirmed its plans to build the UK's largest AI data centre in Loughton, Essex, despite Microsoft's decision to pull out of the project. Microsoft had agreed to fund a supercomputer at the site, but its involvement has been terminated. Nscale is exploring alternative power sources and maintaining a strong relationship with Microsoft for other projects globally. The data centre was expected to receive its power supply by the end of this year, but this has been delayed until the 2030s due to a London-wide grid issue. The project is expected to create 250 permanent jobs when it opens.
